html:
In June 1830 a French army landed at Sidi Ferruch, west of Algiers, and on 5 July the city surrendered. It was the start of 132 years of French rule in Algeria.

The pretext was an insult: in 1827 the dey of Algiers had struck the French consul with a fly whisk in a quarrel over old French debts for grain. King Charles X hoped a victory would win him support at home, but he was overthrown weeks later. The dey went into exile, and the Regency ended.

France spent decades conquering the interior, against the resistance of Emir Abdelkader and others, at a terrible cost to Algerians. Algeria was later made part of France and settled by Europeans (French Algeria), until the war of independence.
